Structure of the plan is sound (MainPage-driven init, capture the delegates, fake args, UI-thread dispatcher). Corrections: (a) Focus is FocusState_Programmatic (3), not Pointer; (b) Enter must be delivered as L"\r\n" in the fake TextBox text (a lone CR is plain text); (c) after any game put_Text the fake must fire TextChanged once (the game sets HID[0x58] before put_Text and only a TextChanged clears it) and TextChanged should be delivered after the setter returns; (d) the pointer handlers are registered from a ThreadPool work item, so the fake ThreadPool must run it and ProcessEvents(2) must return or run on its own thread; (e) the fake SwapChainPanel must also answer get_CompositionScaleX (slot 6) and IUIElement::get_RenderSize (slot 23, used 3x by attachUi 0x1da634 to set client/platform size), the fake DisplayInformation slots 11/12/13; (f) hardware-keyboard path: drop modifier VKs when HID[0x44]==0.

Every slot cross-checked against the SDK 19041 header vtables: ITextBox get_Text 6, put_Text 7, get_MaxLength 14 (used only by the diff 0x1115b0), put_MaxLength 15, put_AcceptsReturn 19, add_TextChanged 30, Select 36 (+0x90); ITextBox2 put_PreventKeyboardDisplayOnProgrammaticFocus 15; IControl Focus 46 (+0xb8, helper 0x11127c, args (FocusState, bool* out)). Both XAML objects are used through QI on the stored IInspectable pointers (HID+0x2c/+0x30), so they need a real QueryInterface for those three IIDs; add_TextChanged takes the delegate and an 8-byte token out buffer (stored at HID+0x38).

The open question/md section 8 says the AppPlatform_Winrt+0x48/+0x4c GetTickCount64 deadline checked by pumpInput (0x50eac) calls a phone StatusBar. It does not: 0x4aeb8 is VibrationDevice.GetDefault (IVibrationDeviceStatics 332FD2F1, string 'Windows.Phone.Devices.Notification.VibrationDevice' at 0x210140), pumpInput calls IVibrationDevice vtable slot 7 (+0x1c = Cancel) when the deadline expires, and the deadline is armed by AppPlatform_Winrt::vibrate (vtable slot 29, 0x51008 calls 0x4aeb8). A fake VibrationDevice with Vibrate(6)/Cancel(7) is what is needed (no status bar involvement).

missing: initInput (0x4b55c) and AttachUi (0x1da634) dependencies not listed: IDisplayInformation slots 12/13 (RawDpiX/RawDpiY) and ISwapChainPanel slot 6 get_CompositionScaleX feed platform+0x38/+0x3c/+0x40; attachUi QIs the SwapChainPanel for IUIElement 676d0be9 and calls get_RenderSize (slot 23) three times to compute client->vtbl[20] (setSize), AppPlatform_Winrt::setScreenWidth (0x4fa40) and 0x4fa20. A fake panel must return a real RenderSize in DIPs before the render loop is started or the game gets a 0x0 viewport.

TextChanged semantics: HID[0x58] is only cleared by the next onTextChanged (and always cleared after the diff by the same handler), so a fake TextBox that does not fire TextChanged after a game put_Text makes the next real keystroke vanish; XAML delivers TextChanged asynchronously and the game relies on that ordering (the CRLF-strip put_Text inside the diff sets 0x58 then the outer handler clears it).
Enter requires an adjacent CR+LF in TextBox.Text (feedChars 0x111894); a lone CR becomes literal text. The finder's plan says L'\r'.

Text typed through the TextBox is injected into the static Keyboard vectors directly from the TextChanged thread (sub_4f5d0 key push, sub_4f648 text push, sub_4d050 backspace) without the platform input queue/critical section; fire TextChanged from one consistent thread (the UI thread) - same as XAML.
FocusState value is Programmatic (3); with PreventKeyboardDisplayOnProgrammaticFocus=false this is the only focus kind the game ever uses, both for show and for hide.

VibrationDevice (not StatusBar) is touched from pumpInput; the fake needs GetDefault statics + Cancel(slot 7), and vibrate() uses Vibrate(slot 6) - belongs to platform_services but pumpInput runs it every frame once armed.

The ThreadPool work item that registers pointer handlers (0x110940) ends with ICoreDispatcher::ProcessEvents(ProcessUntilQuit=2) on the dispatcher of the independent input source; the fake must decide whether that call blocks (own thread) or returns, and must not keep the creating thread inside it.
Moved events with an unknown PointerId insert a std::map node (operator[]); a mouse that only hovers keeps one node for its id. Not harmful but explains stale slot numbers after hover.

Hardware keyboard while the on-screen keyboard is inactive: every unmapped VK (modifiers, CapsLock, OEM keys) becomes a garbage TEXT event on KeyDown; the host must filter to printable letters/digits (or leave HID[0x44]==1 semantics) - the finder mentioned OEM punctuation only.

MinecraftClient::setKeyboardHeight scales the InputPane height twice (platform+0x40 in AppMain::SetKeyboardHeight, then GUI-scale global 0x340d40 in 0x59578): the host should report OccludedRect.Height in DIPs (physical px / composition scale) and then check on screen.

TabTip itself: nothing in the exe talks to TabTip/InputPane.TryShow/TryHide, so show/hide fluctuation must be solved entirely in the host's fake Focus() handling; the level signal available to the host is AppPlatform_Winrt+4 (game intent, set synchronously) vs HID+0x44 (set later inside the UI-thread lambda: 1 after show lambda, 0 at the START of the hide lambda). The two can disagree for one dispatcher round trip; the finder's debounce suggestion is reasonable but unproven.
method: Re-derived with different anchors than the finder: pdata + expected_bytes check for every fact RVA and every 0x1xxxxx RVA in the md; GUID literals decoded from .rdata; vtable slot numbers checked against Windows SDK 19041 headers (windows.ui.core.h, windows.ui.input.h, windows.ui.xaml.controls.h, windows.ui.viewmanagement.h, windows.graphics.display.h) and against the call offsets in the code; handler behaviour by reading the full disassembly of Pressed/Moved/Released/KeyDown/KeyUp, Initialize, the lambdas, onTextChanged and the diff; ordering by reading OnTick/attachUi/initInput/MainPage ctor call sequences; strings by raw ascii/wide search. Area friend_audit was NOT part of this review (the task area is input_text); the only friend_audit statement that touches input (0x1da5b4 is the InputPane keyboard-height setter) was independently confirmed.
